Contents 
 
 
 
TPA / ALTEPLASE (ACTILYSE®) PROTOCOL 
THROMBOLYSIS FOR ST ELEVATION MYOCARDIAL INFARCTION 
 
• 
Provided there are NO contraindications 
 
Absolute Contraindications 
Relative Contraindications 
Any prior intracranial haemorrhage 
History of chronic, severe, poorly 
controlled hypertension 
Known structural cerebral vascular 
lesion e.g. AV malformation 
SBP > 180 mmHg or DBP > 110 mmHg 
Lower BP with nitroglycerin (Nitrocine®) 
infusion 
Known malignant intracranial neoplasm 
Traumatic or prolonged CPR (>10 min) 
NB Consider whether MI may have 
caused the arrest! 
or major surgery (<3 weeks) 
Ischaemic stroke within 3 months 
except acute ischaemic stroke within 3 
hours 
Recent (within 2-4 weeks) internal 
bleeding 
Suspected aortic dissection 
Non-compressible vascular punctures 
Active bleeding or bleeding diathesis 
Pregnancy 
Significant closed head trauma or facial 
trauma within 3 months 
Active peptic ulcer disease (bleed within 
the past 2-4 weeks) 
Current use of anticoagulants e.g. 
Warfarin 
 
• Written and signed consent prior to thrombolysis 
 
 
• Dosage – see package insert for dose/kg 
 
■ 
15 mg IV bolus then 
■ 
0.75 mg/kg over 30 mins (not to exceed 50 mg) then 
■ 
0.5 mg/kg over 60 mins (not to exceed 35 mg) 
 
 
MAXIMUM TOTAL DOSE 100MG 
 
 
• 
Patient requires continuous monitoring – Blood pressure, heart rate, O2 Sats, GCS 
• 
ECG’s to be done at 0 min prior to commencing and then at 15 min, 30 min, 60 min 
and 90 min 
• 
ECG’s also to be done with any rhythm changes or interventions 
• 
Please indicate patients pain score out of 10 on each ECG as well as vital signs 
• 
Reperfusion arrhythmias are common and usually transient and seldom require 
intervention  
 
 
 
 

 
ACUTE HEART FAILURE 
 
GENERAL APPROACH 
• 
Clinical features: Dyspnoea, orthopnoea, effort intolerance, peripheral oedema, PND. Gallop rhythm, 
increased JVP, chest crackles, cardiac murmurs. 
• 
ECG Features: AF, new T wave changes, LVH, LBBB. Noncardiogenic pulm oedema: cerebral T waves 
• 
CXR: pulmonary oedema, pulmonary venous congestion, cardiomegaly, Kerley B lines 
• 
Ultrasound features: > 3 B lines bilaterally, pleural effusions, poor contractility, dilated IVC 
 
• 
Triage to RESUS AREA IF ACUTELY DISTRESSED OR UNSTABLE 
• 
Rapid ABC assessment, IV line, monitors, HGT, VBG, urine ßHCG, ECG 
• 
Correct electrolytes abnormalities 
• 
Crystalloid fluid bolus 10 - 20mg/kg if hypotensive. 
PATIENTS ARE OFTEN INTRAVASCULARLY DEPLETED, DESPITE PERIPHERAL FLUID OVERLOAD 
• 
Comprehensive history and exam, including: 
■ 
Onset, underlying risk factors, likely precipitant. NB prior CCF, ACS history 
■ 
Co-morbidities, chronic medications, compliance 
• 
Document specific ECG changes, POCUS findings 
• 
Further investigations: FBC, U&E, CXR, serial ECGs, troponin, proBNP if diagnosis in doubt 
• 
Differential diagnosis: PE, LRTI, chronic lung disease, fluid overload from other causes e.g. renal/liver 
failure, non-cardiogenic pulmonar
